_comment: Manually authored per-image, per-variant layout. Every crop and text position here is chosen by looking at that specific photo and measuring its actual negative space and subject/product boundaries — nothing here is computed by the renderer. Each top-level key is an image id (must match a key in copy.json); each image has a `master` filename and one or more named variants (e.g. `final`, or `v1`/`v2` while comparing options, or `finalFr` for a locale's own sizing — see references/localization.md). `_notes` fields are free text for a human, ignored by the renderer, and are the right place to record WHY a crop/size was chosen, not just what it is. IMPORTANT: the headlineFontSize values below were measured (via textMetrics.mjs's measureWidth, not guessed) against one specific placeholder headline font at these exact textBox widths — they are a worked example of the fitting PROCESS, not universal numbers. The moment you swap in your real headline font, re-measure every size the same way; a different font's glyphs will be wider or narrower at the same point size.

PRODUCT_001._notes: TEMPLATE_SIDE example. Master is 1200x1500. Subject sits fairly centered/vertical in the frame, so a narrower photo crop still reads well. photoPanelWidthRatio=0.6 on a 1200-wide master gives a 720px photo panel (photoCrop.width) and a 480px panel (canvasWidth-photoPanelWidth); photoCrop.x=180 was chosen by eye to keep the subject inside that 720px window while trimming background on both sides.

PRODUCT_002._notes: TEMPLATE_BOTTOM example. Master is 1200x1500. Composition needs full width to read (subjects/props on both sides), so the photo keeps its full width and only the bottom band is text. photoBandHeightRatio=0.67 gives a photoCrop.height of 1005 (round(1500*0.67)); the panel below (1500-1005=495px tall) holds the text stack.

PRODUCT_003._notes: TEMPLATE_FULL example (used sparingly — only when a photo genuinely has large clean negative space the text can sit in without coming near the subject/product). `crop` here is a plain lossless extract of the master, not a template-ratio panel — its width/height just need to satisfy the canvas aspect check in design-system.json.
